title: Assessment of quality and reliability of YouTube videos for patient and physician education on inflammatory myositis
screen_reason: Cross-sectional content analysis of 453 English-language YouTube videos on myositis (search March 2021). Two physician assessors classified every video as useful / not very useful or misleading / patient narrative, where 'not very useful or misleading' is defined as 'Videos containing clinically incorrect or unproven information based on currently available scientific evidence'. The reported share 1.7% (8/453) is therefore a share of items judged for factual correctness against scientific evidence, i.e. a CONTENT prevalence estimate. The paper additionally reports a second, instrument-based classification (mDISCERN/GQS/JAMA cut-offs) giving 9.0% (41/453) 'not very useful' - that one is a QUALITY row per the review's rule and is kept for the appendix only.

The full sentence is 'Of the analysed videos, 74.3% (337/453) provided infor-/mation that was considered useful and 1.7% (8/453) not very useful.'; the quote starts after the line-break hyphenation because the two-column text rendering interleaves the word 'Discussion' from the adjacent column. estimates.ground_truth_detail: Two authors (MJ, RG), physicians/medical trainees, independently searched and rated every video against the published usefulness definitions; a third independent assessor (LG) resolved conflicts. Reliability reported for the scored instruments only: Cohen's kappa for inter-observer agreement 0.686 (mDISCERN), 0.469 (GQS), 0.537 (JAMA); ICC estimates used for the scale scores. No kappa reported for the usefulness classification itself.
estimates.moderator_quote: we evaluated the quality of videos on YouTube® related to myositis after a thorough search using terms “Myositis”, “Idiopathic Inflammatory Myositis”, “Dermatomyositis”, “Polymyositis”, “Cancer Associated Myositis”, “Inclusion Body Myositis”, “Immune Mediated Necrotizing Myopathy”, “Juvenile Dermatomyositis” and “Overlap Idiopathic Inflammatory Myositis” sequentially in March 2021. ... The first ten pages, i.e. one-hundred videos per search term, were included in the evaluation, as viewers rarely go beyond this. We searched videos using the ‘relevance’ filter, which is the default setting on YouTube®
estimates.notes: Physician-assessed (not score-based) classification. The denominator excludes 372 duplicates, 25 non-English and 50 irrelevant videos from the 900 screened. Rank-truncated (first 100 hits per term, relevance filter), hence denom_selection=curated. The 'unproven' clause and the 'partially misleading' clause make the numerator broader than strictly false content, so breadth=misleading.

estimates.country: Not stated; English-language YouTube videos worldwide (authors in India, UK, USA)
estimates.date: Search conducted March 2021; videos available on 13 March 2021
estimates.measure_type: % of myositis YouTube videos categorised as not very useful by validated-instrument cut-offs (mDISCERN < 4, GQS < 4, JAMA < 3)
estimates.denominator: 453 English-language YouTube videos on myositis analysed
estimates.definition: A video counted for the numerator if it fell below the usefulness cut-offs on the validated scales: modified DISCERN >= 4, GQS >= 4, JAMA >= 3 defined a useful video
estimates.misinfo_def: No falsity definition for this classification; usefulness is defined by score cut-offs on mDISCERN (reliability), the Global Quality Scale and the JAMA benchmark (authorship, attribution, disclosure, currency)
estimates.source_quote: useful and 9.0% (41/453) as not very useful videos, based
estimates.page_loc: Results, 'Agreement', p. 1343; full sentence 'Of the analysed videos, 67.1% (304/453) were categorized as useful and 9.0% (41/453) as not very useful videos, based on the aforementioned criteria.' (quote truncated to the contiguous single-column span). Table 4, p. 1346, lists the study as 'Myositis (current study) | YouTube | 9.05 | 453 | Present study'.
estimates.ground_truth_detail: Scores assigned by the two independent physician assessors using mDISCERN, GQS and the JAMA benchmark criteria; Cohen's kappa for inter-observer agreement 0.686, 0.469 and 0.537 respectively. Agreement with the physicians' own usefulness judgement was poor (combined kappa 0.129; 0.061 mDISCERN, 0.083 GQS, 0.104 JAMA).
estimates.moderator_quote: Reliability was determined using the mDISCERN criteria, quality using the Global Quality Scale (GQS) and JAMA system, using appropriate cut-offs (mDISCERN > 4, GQS > 4, JAMA > 3). ... The cut-off for a useful video was more than or equal to 4 for the modified DISCERN criteria and GQS and more than or equal to 3 for the JAMA scoring system.
estimates.notes: QUALITY, not prevalence: a wholly accurate video can fall below these cut-offs (e.g. by not citing sources or not disclosing authorship), so the label does not certify falsity. The authors nevertheless report this 9.05% as their study's 'Misinformation/low-quality videos (%)' entry in Table 4, which is how the number is likely to be read downstream - flagged for the adjudicator. It disagrees badly with the physicians' own falsity judgement (1.7%), kappa 0.129.

missed_or_uncertain: 1) mDISCERN, GQS and JAMA are also reported as medians (e.g. mDISCERN 4 (3-4) for useful vs 2 (1-3) for not very useful) - scale scores with no share of items, so no row per the instructions. 2) 24% (108/453) patient narratives and 74.3% useful are the complement categories of the extracted CONTENT row and are not separate misinformation estimates. 3) Source-stratified numbers (e.g. 3 of 8 not-very-useful videos from non-medical media, 38%; 'non-medical organizations uploaded the highest proportion of not very useful videos (3/37)') are sub-splits of the 8-video numerator, not headline estimates, so they were not split out; 3/37 = 8.1% of non-medical-media videos is available should the adjudicator want a source-stratified row. 4) Table 4 lists misinformation percentages for ~24 other studies (8.6% Sjogren's, 11.5% SLE, 12.28% gout, 67.2% COVID-19, etc.); all are figures cited from elsewhere and excluded by R8.

rob.design: Cross-sectional YouTube content analysis. Frame: 9 myositis-related search terms run sequentially in March 2021 in incognito mode with cookies/history cleared, default 'relevance' filter, first 10 pages (100 videos) per term = 900 videos screened; exclusions 372 duplicates, 25 non-English, 50 irrelevant, leaving 453. Coding: two authors (MJ, RG) independently viewed and rated every video on 21 characteristics plus usefulness category, mDISCERN, GQS and JAMA; a third author (LG) adjudicated disagreements. Reliability: ICC (two-way mixed, absolute agreement, k = 3) for the scales; Cohen's kappa 0.686 (mDISCERN), 0.469 (GQS), 0.537 (JAMA); no reliability statistic for the usefulness classification. Limitations acknowledged: English only, single platform, first 100 results only, cross-sectional snapshot of a changing platform.
